findings.claim: The prompt tells the Engineer to take the argv for lint, build and unit_test from the steps of the `check` script. In package.json:15, `check` has six `pnpm --filter <app> lint` steps. It has seven build steps, and `@detran/ui` and `@detran/boat-mobile` each appear twice. It has seven test steps, including `@detran/ui test`. The root `build` script (package.json:21, backend) is not part of the CTG-0004 contract. The prompt does not say whether each kind gets the ordered list of all matching steps or a single step, so the Engineer could pick one app or use the root `build`, and the per-kind link would be incomplete.
findings.fix: Add: for each kind, record the ordered list of every `pnpm --filter … lint|build|test` step in `check`, deduplicated, and do not use the root `build` script. If one argv per SensorReading cannot represent the set, mark it `source_pending` and report it. Do not pick a representative step.

findings.claim: The prompt forbids running protected verbs during the task (line 51) and requires a consent flag, but it never defines 'protected verb'. Under the registry, running `devai sense run --preset baseline` without `--write` still runs `build` (local-write) and `unit_test` (harness-write). The Engineer could treat `pnpm devai:sense --preset baseline` as a harmless manual check.
findings.fix: Define protected verbs as any real call to `devai sense run`/`sense record` and any kind whose effect is not `read`. During the task, validation happens only through `node --test` with an injected `execute` and `pnpm devai:sense` with no parameters. Never run the CLI with `--preset`.
